Strait of Hormuz Status: October 15, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  228 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
15 October 2026 .
Brent $ 104.19 -1.87 % · Transits 2 (2026-10-11) · AI-assisted
01 CNN reports two cargo ships have sunk in the Strait of Hormuz as Iran ramps up attacks in the run-up to the US midterm elections.

02 Attacks on ships in the strait have reached their highest level since the start of the war, per ABC News and the Australian Broadcasting Corporation.

03 Brent stood at $104.19, down 1.87% over 24 hours, as of 06:09 UTC.

Situation
ABC News and the Australian Broadcasting Corporation report that attacks on ships have reached their highest level since the start of the war. The Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride, carrying more than 2,500 containers, sank near the strait; MarineLink reports that the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore said two Singapore-registered vessels were struck by unknown projectiles while transiting, one sinking after catching fire and the other sustaining hull damage, with the GFS Pride identified as the vessel lost. The IRGC says the GFS Pride struck a mine; maritime security sources told Reuters she sank after a projectile hit her. No maritime authority has reconciled the two accounts. Lloyd's List reports a containership sank as attacks on shipping intensify, and Iran is reported to have changed its interdiction tactics, with Deccan Herald noting oil prices have climbed as Iran deploys new methods to target transiting vessels. Iran has struck 12 ships in four days, no major wire in this feed carries that figure independently. IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent stood at $104.19, down 1.87% over 24 hours, as of 06:09 UTC. The feed indexed 124 headlines in the past 24 hours. As of 06:22 UTC, 131 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, flat over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
